entry.title: HackerTube
entry.content:
It was Friday night at 11pm, I was tired, I went to YouTube to watch something and realized that I was looking at an enshittified wall of slop. Insanely exaggerated thumbnails, dumb recommendations of the same tired topics, truly terrible idiocracy-grade content. I'm sure this algorithm works well for the median person on the internet, but it definitely does not work for me. So this morning (Saturday) I took a hold of my Opus 5.5 and gave it the task: Let's write our own YouTube clone based on whatever videos have been recommended on Hacker News. And Opus came back with: hackertube.org!

Opus downloaded all comments of HackerNews, filtered them, ran Sonnet over them in a Workflow (Claude Code feature), got rid of spam, and narrowed everything down to 40K comments recommending a YouTube video. In total, we get 6,454 YouTube videos that have been recommended by a few people on HN from 2007-2026 across 150 topics. Then we wrap it up in a YouTube UI, get a domain, push to a VPS, secure, harden, optimize and voila!

HackerTube:

  • Contains quality content
  • Uses the 50% thumbnail instead of the uploaded thumbnail

entry.title: Sequoia Ascent 2026 summary
entry.summary: Summary of my talk at Sequoia Ascent
entry.content:
I did a fireside chat at Sequoia Ascent 2026. The YouTube video is here:

YouTube Video Link

As an experiment, I fed an LLM all of my recent blog posts and tweets, then I had it read this video's transcript and produce 1) a summary and 2) a cleaned up transcript (correcting all transcription mistakes, getting rid of fill words, etc). I am posting both of these below. These can be useful for both people who may want to just read the summary in text format, but also for LLMs so that my content is legible and available to them.

AI generated content below for this talk follows. I used a top capability model (in this case Codex 5.5) and read the content and it reads ok without glaring mistakes.

Sequoia Ascent 2026: Software 3.0, Agentic Engineering, and Jagged Intelligence

I recently joined Stephanie Zhan for a fireside chat at Sequoia Ascent 2026, speaking with founders about the recent shift in AI agents, what it means for software, and how I think about the next wave of AI-native companies.
